key_points: Small-bore chest tubes (≤14 F) are effective for most pleural drainage indications with better tolerability than large-bore tubes.
Ultrasound guidance is the modality of choice for site selection and has become the standard of care for SBCT placement.
Common SBCT indications include pleural infection, malignant pleural effusion, pneumothorax, and selected hemothorax scenarios.
Seldinger technique is the preferred insertion method; trocar insertion should generally be avoided due to organ injury risk.
Routine suction is not recommended for pneumothorax management; water seal often suffices.
Complication rates are low with image guidance and experienced operators; major complications are rare.

structures: Chest wall (pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi, intercostal spaces)
Internal mammary, subclavian, axillary vessels (avoidance landmarks)

clinical_procedures: Pre-procedure preparation: imaging review, coagulation/anticoagulant assessment, consent, monitoring setup, checklist completion.
Ultrasound mapping: identify largest/optimal pocket, mark insertion site; assess effusion complexity/loculation or absence of lung sliding.
Patient positioning: seated with ipsilateral arm supported or lateral decubitus with affected side up.
SBCT insertion (Seldinger): anesthetize, needle entry just superior to rib, guidewire, small incision, serial dilation, catheter over wire, connect and secure, confirm with chest radiograph.
Site selection principles: lateral placement to improve comfort and minimize kinking; avoid posterior 6 cm from spine; avoid major vessels.
Pleural drainage systems: collection chamber, water seal, suction control (wet or dry); consider modern digital suction for quantifying air leak.
Removal: criteria by indication (no air leak, full expansion; or output <100–200 mL/24 h); Valsalva/expiration during removal; seal with petroleum gauze.
diagnostic_approaches: Ultrasound as first-line imaging to guide SBCT site selection and reduce complications.
Fluoroscopy or CT guidance when indicated (complex collections, post-surgical anatomy).
Radiographic confirmation post-placement to verify position and lung expansion.
treatment_algorithms: Pleural infection: early antibiotics plus image-guided SBCT drainage; consider intrapleural fibrinolytics (alteplase) plus DNase if initial drainage fails; surgical referral based on response.
Malignant pleural effusion: inpatient symptomatic drainage via SBCT; talc slurry pleurodesis through SBCT or talc poudrage during thoracoscopy; success rates similar across SBCT vs large-bore.

Pneumothorax: conservative management for minimally symptomatic PSP; if intervention needed, SBCT appropriate in most cases; reserve large-bore for substantial air leak, trauma, mechanical ventilation, or unstable tension pneumothorax.
Hemothorax: stable patients may be managed effectively with ~14 F SBCT; unstable traumatic hemothorax favors larger-bore for rapid flow; >28 F rarely adds benefit.
Suction policy: avoid routine suction for pneumothorax; consider water seal unless specific indications for suction exist.
clinical_guidelines: Use ultrasound guidance for pleural procedures and SBCT insertion.
Prefer small-bore tubes for most indications to improve comfort without compromising outcomes.
Avoid routine suction for pneumothorax; use water seal unless otherwise indicated.
Consider ambulatory drains selectively in reliable PSP patients with close follow-up; not recommended for symptomatic secondary SP.
drug_information: Local anesthetic: Lidocaine 1–2% (10–20 mL) for skin, subcutaneous tissue, periosteum, and parietal pleura during SBCT insertion.
Intrapleural agents (when indicated): Alteplase plus DNase for pleural infection; graded sterile talc (e.g., 4 g) for pleurodesis via slurry.

tables.title: Small-bore chest tube insertion by Seldinger technique (stepwise)
rows: Review indication, imaging, blood work; consent; monitoring ready; pre-procedure checklist.
Position patient to optimize access (seated with arm supported or lateral decubitus).
Ultrasound the thorax; mark entry site.
Sterile prep and drape; full barrier precautions.
Local anesthesia: 10–20 mL lidocaine 1–2%—skin wheal, deeper tissues, periosteum, parietal pleura.
Introduce needle just superior to the rib; confirm pleural entry with aspiration.
Advance guidewire; maintain ≥15–20 cm externally; remove needle.
Serial dilation over guidewire through subcutaneous tissue and parietal pleura.
Advance SBCT over guidewire; remove guidewire.
Connect to drainage system; secure with 1–2 sutures; apply dressing.
Post-procedure chest radiograph to confirm placement and lung expansion.

definitions.definition: Chest drain of ≤14 French used for pleural evacuation of air or fluid.
Guidewire-assisted catheter insertion method for safe pleural access.
Direct tube insertion over a rigid trocar; faster but higher organ-injury risk—generally avoided.
One-way valve allowing air egress for ambulatory management of air leaks.
One-way mechanism preventing return of air into pleural space during inspiration.
Electronic system providing controlled suction and quantifying air leak.
Acute pulmonary edema following rapid lung re-expansion; uncommon but potentially serious.
Traditional landmarked zone for tube insertion; modern practice favors ultrasound-guided lateral placement.
Flow ∝ radius^4 and inversely ∝ viscosity; informs tube-size selection for high-flow/viscous drainage.

clinical_pearls: Insert as lateral as comfortable to reduce pain and kinking; avoid posterior strip within ~6 cm of the spine where intercostal arteries may vary.
Enter just superior to the rib to avoid the intercostal neurovascular bundle.
Favor Seldinger over trocar for safety; reserve trocar for emergencies only.
Do not routinely apply suction for pneumothorax; water seal often suffices and may limit fistula propagation.
Clamp trials may be used selectively prior to removal in pneumothorax to detect intermittent leaks.
references: BTS Pleural Disease Guideline 2023 – pleural procedures, ultrasound guidance, suction recommendations.
Prospective and randomized data on SBCT vs large-bore in hemothorax/trauma – equivalence in evacuation with better comfort for 14 F in stable patients.
RAPID risk model and management flow for pleural infection; consensus on tPA/DNase.
Randomized trials AMPLE and TIME2 – IPC vs talc pleurodesis in MPE.
NEJM 2020 – Conservative vs interventional treatment for PSP; ambulatory trials for PSP; joint ERS/EACTS/ESTS guidance on SP.

clinical_applications: Use SBCTs as first-line drains for pleural infection, MPE (inpatient drainage or talc slurry pleurodesis), most pneumothoraces requiring intervention, and selected hemothorax cases.
Adopt ultrasound as standard for site selection; consider digital devices to quantify air leak when available.
practice_recommendations: Default to Seldinger insertion with full barrier precautions and lateral site selection.
Reserve large-bore tubes for unstable traumatic hemothorax, substantial air leak, post-thoracic surgery, or ventilated patients when high flow is imperative.
Avoid routine suction for pneumothorax and monitor closely for RPE during rapid drainage of large effusions.
future_directions: Head-to-head trials of suction vs water seal in pneumothorax with standardized digital air-leak metrics.
Optimal SBCT size selection frameworks incorporating viscosity/flow modeling for diverse clinical scenarios.
controversies: Ambulatory management appropriateness for SSP versus PSP.
Thresholds for tube upsizing or surgical referral in complicated infection or persistent air leak.

points: Image-guided SBCT placement is safe and effective for most pleural drainage indications with outcomes comparable to large-bore tubes.
Seldinger technique and ultrasound guidance are central to maximizing success and minimizing complications.
Selective suction use and careful removal criteria improve safety; major complications remain uncommon with best practices.

seldinger_steps: Checklist, consent, monitoring, position, ultrasound marking.
Sterile prep and drape; anesthetize skin to pleura with lidocaine.
Needle entry just superior to rib; confirm pleural entry by aspiration.
Guidewire advancement; remove needle; skin incision; serial dilation.
Advance SBCT over wire; connect, secure, dress; confirm with chest radiograph.
